items.title: Knicks Hoping For Karl-Anthony Towns Extension Closer To $200M Over Four Years
items.summary: The New York Knicks are navigating a challenging contract extension discussion with Karl-Anthony Towns and are significantly apart on a new number. The Knicks are "far more interested" in signing Towns to a contract closer to a four-year, $200 million deal compared to the four-year, $276 million extension he is eligible to sign, reports Jake Fischer at Bleacher Report . Towns is prepared to sign for less than his max, but the two sides are significantly apart on value. Towns can become a free agent during the 2027 offseason if they are unable to agree to terms on an extension. The Knicks are facing ongoing second apron issues and hope to bring down his 2027-28 player option worth $61 million. Towns is set to come off his four-year, $220 million supermax extension signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2022. Towns was an All-NBA player in his first season with the Knicks and was critical in their 2026 championship.

items.summary: The New York Knicks announced a series of transactions, as they continue tinkering with their training camp roster. New York waived John Konchar and N'Faly Dante, who had been signed to non-guaranteed camp deals. The Knicks signed Jaden Akins to a two-way deal, after signing-and-waiving him twice previously this offseason. New York also signed veteran center Tony Bradley to a training camp deal. In addition, the Knicks signed-and-waived Toby Okani. This was done in order to meet roster minimum requirements while making their other transactions. Okani is expected to join the Westchester Knicks for the G League season.

items.title: Karl-Anthony Towns Wants Knicks Extension, Admits Discomfort Of Open Contract
items.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns reiterated Monday that he wants a contract extension with the New York Knicks, while acknowledging the discomfort of an unsettled deal as the team defends its NBA title. Towns spoke at the Knicks' media day. "I've made it known I want to play here," said Towns. "I've been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible." Towns is eligible for a four-year extension worth more than $276 million, but an agreement before the season does not appear likely . Towns is owed $57 million this season and holds a $61.1 million player option for next year. Asked whether he would prefer to table talks once the season begins to avoid a distraction, Towns said comfort is not part of the equation. "In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had," said Towns. Towns averaged 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists last season as New York won its first title in 53 years with a five-game Finals victory over the San Antonio Spurs. Towns turns 31 in November. The Towns extension talks are an inflection point in keeping the championship core together and also staying below the second apron. That constraint has already cost the Knicks backup center Mitchell Robinson, who signed with the Boston Celtics this summer. Towns said he leaves the financial mechanics to team president Leon Rose. "You ask me to give three facts or two facts about the second apron, I can't do it," said Towns. "I have no interest in that. It is what it is. Leon trusts me with stuff on the court, and I trust him with that stuff." Towns said the team will address the topic openly during the season. "The first thing is we try to talk about everything. We don't leave any elephants in the room," said Towns. "They'll figure it out and our group has done a fantastic job of understanding that we can only control what we can control." Josh Hart is also eligible for an extension with the Knicks. He will earn $20.9 million this season, and the Knicks hold a $22.3 million team option for 2027-28. Hart said uncertainty can wear on players. "When there's uncertainty, there's gonna be a lot of questions," said Hart. "Rumors and at a human level it can wear people down and it can affect how you handle business on a daily basis. You want to get it done so you don't have to deal with that. At the end of the day, it's a business. For me, as long as I'm wearing this jersey, I'm going to play as hard as I can. Hopefully we can figure that out."
